messages.author: 80be28d1c34430a5
messages.subject: GcRmaBackgroundCorrection for custom array
parts:
Hi Henrik,

I'm attempting to use aroma.affymetrix in analysing a custom array -
PFSANGER - on which you have answered some questions before. It's a
tiling-like (unique probes only) array for plasmodium. I have been
able to create a ugp file to read in probe positions on the
chromosome. I have been unable to figure out how to input the probe
sequences into aroma so I can perform GCRma background correction. I
have the sequences and their corresponding probe names in a file but
am not sure what format is required. Is this possible to do?

Regards,
Ben

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] GcRmaBackgroundCorrection for custom array
parts:
On Wed, May 21, 2008 at 12:44 AM, Benjamin <ben.la...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Henrik,
>
> I'm attempting to use aroma.affymetrix in analysing a custom array -
> PFSANGER - on which you have answered some questions before. It's a
> tiling-like (unique probes only) array for plasmodium. I have been
> able to create a ugp file to read in probe positions on the
> chromosome.

Note that the UGP file contains (chromsome, position) for the units
not the individual probes (unless you have one probe per unit). The
units are defined by the CDF you are using.

> I have been unable to figure out how to input the probe
> sequences into aroma so I can perform GCRma background correction. I
> have the sequences and their corresponding probe names in a file but
> am not sure what format is required. Is this possible to do?

First of all, it was Ken Simpson that did most of the work of porting
(wrapping) GcRmaBackgroundCorrection to aroma.affymetrix. I am a bit
rusty on the details and I don't use gcRMA bg correction myself so the
class is probably a bit rusty as well. However, we do test
GcRmaBackgroundCorrection for 'HG-U133_Plus_2' is our redundancy tests
so it does work.

To start, you need to put a file named <chip type>_probe_tab in the
corresponding chip type directory, e.g.
annotationData/chipType/PFSANGER/PFSANGER_probe_tab. If you do
process(bg, verbose=-20) you will see if it is found or not; the
located file will be displayed.

Having a quick look at computeAffinities() of AffymetrixCdfFile, which
is the method querying the probe_tab file, one see that the first
column must contain unit names. Then the code tries to identify the
column containing the sequences by looking at the data (not the
header) for pattern "[actgACTG]{25}". It next tries to locate column
(x,y) by pattern "[0-9][0-9]*". It then matches unit names in the
probe_tab file with the unit names in the corresponding CDF. It a
name is not found in the CDF, an exception is thrown. ...then there
is much more following... Please see the code,
print(computeAffinities.AffymetrixCdfFile), if you have problems.
Make sure to use verbose.

FYI, for 'HG-U133_Plus_2' we use Affymetrix probe_tab file named
'HG-U133-PLUS_probe_tab' [although Affymetrix don't use filename
format <chip type>_probe_tab, you should]. It contents is:

Probe Set Name<tab>Probe X<tab>Probe Y<tab>Probe Interrogation
Position<tab>Probe Sequence<tab>Target Strandedness
1007_s_at<tab>718<tab>317<tab>3330<tab>CACCCAGCTGGTCCTGTGGATGGGA<tab>Antisense
1007_s_at<tab>1105<tab>483<tab>3443<tab>GCCCCACTGGACAACACTGATTCCT<tab>Antisense
...

Hope this get you started.

/Henrik

>
> Regards,
> Ben
> >
>

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: GcRmaBackgroundCorrection for custom array
parts:
Hi Ben,

Sorry to hear you are having problems with GCRMA background correction.

It's possible that changes to the GCRMA code since I originally wrote
the wrapper for aroma.affymetrix have led to some incompatibility. I
will try to have a look at it in the next day or so but since it is
more than a year since I looked at the package (i'm no longer in
science) it might take me a little while to resolve. In the meantime
you might like to try running the code with a test set of hg-u133 data
(eg from affy's website) to see if you get the same error, since
original testing was mostly done with that chip IIRC.

Cheers,

Ken

parts:
Hi,

thanks for looking into this Ken. Yes, it might be that recent
changes in the underlying 'gcrma' package cause the problem - there
has been a few message on Bioconductor reporting problem with gcrma.

FYI/FAI, the following test script is part of the redundancy tests
that aroma.affymetrix do pass:

path <- system.file("testScripts/system/chipTypes/HG-U133_Plus_2",
package="aroma.affymetrix");
filename <- "test20070824,HG-U133_Plus_2,bg.R";
pathname <- file.path(path, filename);
file.show(pathname);

[BEGIN]
library(aroma.affymetrix);

log <- Verbose(threshold=-4);
timestampOn(log);

dataSetName <- "Affymetrix-HeartBrain";
chipType <- "HG-U133_Plus_2";

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(dataSetName, chipType=chipType, verbose=log);
print(cs);

bg <- GcRmaBackgroundCorrection(cs);
print(bg);
csBg <- process(bg, verbose=log);
[END]

In addition to the data set, it requires
'annotationData/chipTypes/HG-U133_Plus_2/HG-U133-PLUS_probe_tab'
[35,898,262 bytes].

So at least GcRmaBackgroundCorrection works here with the default settings.

One thing to improve the code more robust is to add a lot of internal
validations/asserts to test the sanity of intermediate data objects.
With that in hand it will be easier to spot where something goes
wrong. I add this where ever I can and I can have a look at the above
as well, but it will take some time (weeks?).

Cheers

Henrik
